plan.interpretation: The gap between 19th St and 12th St — six points of on-time performance with nearly identical factors on their rows — suggests something station-specific is happening at 19th. It could be platform layout, stairwell bottlenecks, or how the crowd from events and the game converges at that particular stop. The rebase means I can't compare to prior cycles, but the station-to-station comparison within this cycle is valid and points to a real operational question.
unverifiedLead: Possible that 19th St's lower on-time is tied to the Baylight construction-active factor affecting the station approach differently than at 12th St
Possible that the game-day crowd from Downtown and the event crowd from Lake Merritt converge at 19th St in a way they don't at 12th St, creating a compounding effect
Possible that the station's physical layout — narrow platforms or single choke point — amplifies dwell time when ridership peaks
